item.title: This Australian Luxury Travel Collection Is Opening New Doors to the Country’s Most Extraordinary Landscapes in 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From the Great Barrier Reef and Tasmania’s Freycinet Peninsula to Western Australia’s Ningaloo Coast and the remote East Kimberley, a series of major investments is reshaping the future of luxury wilderness travel across Australia. Members of Luxury Lodges of Australia are preparing a new chapter of openings, refurbishments, private accommodations, and small-ship expeditions throughout 2027. Orpheus Island Lodge has already reopened following an extensive refurbishment, while Saffire Freycinet will introduce Saffire Jewel, an expansive private villa designed for families and small groups, in December 2026. Further ahead, Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef is scheduled to reopen in March 2027 with refreshed eco-luxury wilderness tents and guest spaces, followed by the May reopening of Bullo River Station after a major redevelopment of its remote outback homestead. May also marks the 40th anniversary of True North Adventure Cruises, which will introduce new expeditions exploring Western Australia’s Rowley Shoals and the Great Barrier Reef. Together, these developments offer fresh reasons to plan a luxury Australia itinerary built around extraordinary landscapes, private guiding, marine encounters, and access to places far beyond the usual travel routes.

The Curated Take

Australia’s most compelling luxury experiences often begin where conventional travel becomes more difficult. What distinguishes this collection is not simply the standard of its accommodations, but the access each property provides to a particular landscape, community, or ecosystem. From the marine wilderness of Ningaloo and the Great Barrier Reef to Tasmania’s dramatic coastline and the vast cattle country of the Kimberley, these investments reinforce the appeal of journeys shaped by place rather than a checklist of destinations. For travelers considering Australia in 2027, the developments also create an opportunity to combine several distinct lodge experiences into one richly varied journey.

item.title: This Los Cabos Resort Is Bringing Mexican Traditions and Family Celebrations to Thanksgiving
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Thanksgiving takes on a distinctly Baja California character at Las Ventanas al Paraíso, A Rosewood Resort, where a weeklong Season of Gratitude from November 21–28, 2026, brings families together through regional traditions, culinary experiences, and time along the coast. At the center of the celebrations is a Thanksgiving dinner at Alebrije, featuring a family-style menu that brings together holiday favorites, French and Italian influences, and ingredients from local producers. Beyond the table, the program invites guests of different generations to take part in Mexican craft activities, traditional Lotería, cooking challenges, and garden explorations. Teenagers have their own creative and social experiences, while families can enjoy beach activities, evening s’mores, stargazing, and a movie night beneath the coastal sky. Set where the desert landscape meets the Sea of Cortez, the resort offers a festive holiday escape shaped by food, culture, and shared experiences.

The Curated Take

Thanksgiving travel can be about more than recreating the familiar holiday somewhere warmer. Las Ventanas al Paraíso offers a different way to celebrate, bringing Mexican traditions and local ingredients into a gathering that still honors the pleasures of the Thanksgiving table. The multigenerational programming is particularly appealing, giving children, teenagers, and adults their own ways to participate while creating opportunities to come together. For families considering a luxury Thanksgiving getaway in Los Cabos, the experience makes the holiday feel both recognizable and refreshingly connected to its setting.

item.title: Where to Get Merry This Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The holiday season has a way of bringing familiar traditions back into focus, but there’s something special about experiencing them somewhere new. Perhaps it’s a Christmas tree lighting in a mountain village, an evening spent wandering beneath illuminated Alpine facades, or the excitement of waking up on Christmas morning in a centuries-old Irish castle. Across the U.S. and Europe, hotels and resorts are finding their own ways to celebrate, pairing seasonal traditions with distinctive experiences that make the holidays worth traveling for.

Whether the plan is a family escape, a romantic winter retreat, or simply an excuse to extend the celebrations beyond home, here are a few places to get merry this holiday season.

A Season of Lights in the Swiss Alps

In the Swiss Alpine village of Évolène, the holiday season brings a particularly enchanting reason to step outside after dark. From December 6 through January 6, Évolène en Lumière transforms Rue Centrale into an illuminated celebration of local heritage. Each evening from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m., light and music projections bring the historic village facades, including the church, to life. Lighting installations throughout the village tell stories drawn from regional traditions and local mythology, creating an immersive walk through the area’s cultural history.

Guests staying at Le Rucher d’Évolène can also enjoy the seasonal atmosphere surrounding the new Hôtel Le Central, where a charming Christmas market takes place on the church square. With the market directly in front of the hotel, the village’s festive traditions are never far away.

A Handmade Christmas Above Lake Lucerne

A little higher above the water, Bürgenstock Resort celebrates the season with A Handmade Christmas, a December program centered on craftsmanship, creativity, and time together. Rather than simply decorating for the holidays, the resort invites guests to take part in them through wreath-making, pottery, painting, baking workshops, and miniature Christmas tree decorating.

The experience extends outdoors, too. Torchlit hikes accompanied by Glühwein and roasted chestnuts offer a distinctly Alpine way to spend a winter evening, while families can look forward to Christmas films, craft activities, outdoor adventures, and a visit from Santa on Christmas Eve.

For those looking to make the occasion a longer escape, two festive packages offer different interpretations of a Swiss Christmas. Legendary Christmas includes a decorated in-suite Christmas tree, a champagne welcome, and a private cinema experience complete with Christmas cookies, popcorn, and hot chocolate. A Winter Getaway takes a more adventurous approach, bringing guests into the mountains by 4x4 or snowmobile before a snowshoe journey through snow-covered forests to a local farm for lunch with a farming family. Both packages include breakfast, Alpine Spa access, and use of the resort’s funicular and catamaran.

As the year draws to a close, five distinct dining experiences across the mountain provide options for New Year’s Eve, with menus ranging from contemporary Asian and Persian cuisine to traditional Swiss Fondue Chinoise.

A White Christmas in the Austrian Alps

In Oberlech, Austria, where the village is car-free, Christmas at Burg Hotel Lech is shaped by the traditions of a family-run Alpine retreat. Christmas Eve begins with carols in the lobby, led by the Lucian family and accompanied by the Mozarteum Salzburg String Quartet. Santa Claus makes an appearance with gifts for younger guests, while the quartet continues playing through Christmas dinner.

The festivities extend throughout Advent with surprises waiting behind the doors of the hotel’s Burg Advent Calendar. And when Christmas gives way to the new year, the celebrations continue with a New Year’s Eve party and live DJ, welcoming 2027 in distinctly festive fashion.

Winter Evenings at Forsthofgut Nature Hotel

At Forsthofgut Nature Hotel in Leogang, Austria, winter is an invitation to slow down and settle into the pleasures of the season. A new outdoor ice rink overlooking the Leoganger Steinberge offers a scenic setting for skating, while the slopeside setting of Restaurant 1617 brings guests closer to the mountain atmosphere.

After time on the ice, guests can warm up with mulled wine, hot chocolate, and roasted chestnuts before gathering around the fireplace for Austrian specialties and fondue. Cheese, meat, and chocolate variations are served in wood-paneled dining rooms warmed by tiled stoves and open fireplaces.

The hotel’s Looking Forward to Christmas package adds a seasonal touch to a winter stay, with homemade Christmas cookies and a spa treatment. Available November 28 through December 19, the package offers three- to seven-night stays.

Holiday Traditions and a Little Christmas Magic in Michigan

Not every holiday escape requires a trip across the Atlantic. At Saint John’s Resort in Michigan, the season unfolds with a lineup of celebrations designed to bring families together.

The festivities begin with a Thanksgiving feast on November 26 in the resort’s Monarch Ballroom, where guests can enjoy traditional holiday favorites alongside more indulgent offerings, including corn-manchego pudding, sourdough bread stuffing, turkey and prime rib carving stations, and an interactive pie and cheesecake station.

The following evening, November 27, the Monarch Courtyard hosts the resort’s Christmas tree lighting. Thousands of twinkling lights, live carolers, hot cocoa, and a gathering around the fire set the tone for the weeks ahead.

Families with younger children may especially enjoy the resort’s A Very Merry Holiday Sleepover Package, available December 4, 11, and 18. The evening begins with an in-room visit from one of Santa’s elves, complete with a children’s book and sweet treat before bedtime. The following morning brings breakfast at FIVE Steakhouse, accompanied by a $100 dining credit, and a special visit from Santa.

For those who prefer to save their celebration for the final night of the year, The Wine Grotto hosts a New Year’s Eve gathering with an expansive buffet featuring charcuterie, fresh seafood, and a New York strip carving station, alongside music and an open bar.

A Winter Wonderland in Stowe, Vermont

At the base of Mount Mansfield, The Lodge at Spruce Peak brings together the pleasures of a mountain winter and the traditions of the holiday season. As Stowe Mountain Resort opens for skiing in November, guests have direct access to the slopes, along with the restaurants, outdoor activities, and village celebrations that make Spruce Peak a destination in its own right.

The holiday calendar begins with Thanksgiving dinner on November 26, followed by the return of Mistletoe’s Holiday Bar on November 27. Throughout December, the resort adds seasonal touches to the experience, from Saturday ramen lunches at Tipsy Trout to the Holiday Retreat Weekend on December 4 and 5, featuring culinary experiences and festive activities.

Families can join the Holiday Gnome Hunt beginning December 18, following clues throughout Spruce Peak Village in search of hidden gnomes and a prize. The annual Spruce Peak Lights Festival follows on December 19, bringing Ice Dance International’s Holiday on Ice, photos with Santa, and additional village celebrations.

Christmas week includes afternoon tea on Christmas Eve and a Christmas Day dinner buffet. The celebrations continue on December 26 with an Oyster Takeover and a Holiday Hits Glow Skate Party at the resort’s nearly 10,000-square-foot outdoor ice rink.

For New Year’s Eve, the festivities extend across the mountain, with dinner and a countdown party at The Lodge, followed by the village’s Fire & Ice celebration, featuring Ice Dance International and fireworks over the mountain. Between skiing, skating, snowshoeing, Nordic skiing, and warming up with a whiskey cocktail or raclette at the WhistlePig Pavilion, there is plenty to keep winter visitors entertained well beyond the holiday table.

An Irish Christmas at Lough Eske Castle

In Donegal, Ireland, Lough Eske Castle offers a Christmas rooted in the traditions of a grand 19th-century castle. The four-night festive program, running December 23 through 26, brings together seasonal dining, live music, family activities, and the familiar rituals that make Christmas feel like Christmas.

Guests arrive on December 23 before the celebrations begin on Christmas Eve with a three-course dinner at Cedars Restaurant or the Gallery Bar, followed by mulled wine and mince pies in the castle’s main foyer. Live music in the Gallery Bar sets the tone for the evening.

Christmas Day begins with a full Irish breakfast in Cedars Restaurant, followed by a festive buffet lunch in the Castle Ballroom. The evening continues with a Christmas Night Buffet Supper in the Gallery Bar, accompanied by live entertainment. On December 26, St. Stephen’s Day, guests can enjoy another leisurely breakfast, time to explore the castle grounds, a three-course dinner, and an additional evening of music.

Younger guests have their own celebrations, including Santa’s Little Helpers activities on Christmas Eve, a visit from Santa on Christmas Day, a festive fairy trail, and seasonal activities throughout the stay. Earlier in December, the castle also hosts its Children’s Teddy Bear Afternoon Tea Party, December 13 through 20, combining festive treats with a Christmas disco and a special visit from Santa.

The season officially begins November 29 with the castle’s annual Christmas Lighting Ceremony. Alongside the lighting, children can enjoy a festive disco in the Grand Ballroom. The event also launches the castle’s annual St. Vincent de Paul Christmas charity food drive, supporting local families. It’s a reminder that some of the most meaningful holiday traditions extend beyond the guests staying within the castle walls.

item.title: This Bali Cliffside Resort Is Creating a New Setting for Destination Weddings in 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Overlooking the Indian Ocean from Bali’s dramatic Uluwatu coastline, Karma Kandara is introducing a 2027 collection of bespoke wedding and celebration experiences designed around the island’s natural beauty. The portfolio encompasses everything from intimate proposals and pre-wedding photography to beachfront ceremonies and clifftop receptions, with four distinctive settings: the ocean-facing Sarang Lounge, the resort’s Main Infinity Pool, di Mare Restaurant, and the white sands of Karma Beach Bali. Couples can envision a barefoot celebration beside the sea, an elegant reception framed by panoramic ocean views, or a striking ceremony staged above the water. Beyond weddings, the collection also accommodates milestone occasions and private gatherings, with tailored event planning and experiences that make the most of Uluwatu’s coastal landscape.

The Curated Take

A destination wedding becomes more meaningful when its setting feels inseparable from the place itself. At Karma Kandara, the contrast between white-sand shoreline, dramatic cliffs, and expansive ocean views gives couples several ways to shape a celebration around Bali rather than simply bring a wedding format somewhere tropical. The range of venues also makes the resort worth considering for couples seeking an intimate gathering or a larger celebration, with the Indian Ocean providing a memorable backdrop at every scale.

item.title: Beyond the Ballroom: W Kuala Lumpur Is Bringing a Bold New Energy to Luxury Events
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the heart of Malaysia’s capital, W Kuala Lumpur is positioning meetings, corporate retreats, and private celebrations as experiences in their own right. Blending contemporary design, personalised service, creative culinary offerings, and a distinctive lifestyle sensibility, the hotel brings a fresh perspective to luxury event planning. Its versatile spaces accommodate everything from executive meetings and conferences to gala dinners, brand launches, and social gatherings, with bespoke menus, immersive themes, and entertainment tailored to each occasion. Event organisers also benefit from streamlined group accommodation through Marriott’s ResLink booking platform, while the hotel’s W Insider offers connections to Kuala Lumpur’s art, music, fashion, dining, and nightlife scenes. Sustainability is another part of the approach, with initiatives that include locally sourced ingredients, plant-forward menus, reduced single-use plastics, and more responsible waste management. For eligible 2027 group stays and catering events booked by December 31, 2026, the hotel is also offering special Marriott Bonvoy incentives.

The Curated Take

The most memorable gatherings often extend beyond the event itself, and W Kuala Lumpur understands the value of giving guests a sense of the destination alongside a well-designed meeting or celebration. Its combination of contemporary hospitality, distinctive dining, and access to the city’s cultural scene makes it an interesting choice for planners seeking something more expressive than a conventional business hotel. The emphasis on conscious event practices adds another consideration for organizations looking to bring their values into the way they meet and celebrate.

item.title: Chiva-Som Hua Hin: The Art of Wellness Begins with Listening
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Chiva-Som Hua Hin, wellness is approached as a deeply personal practice, shaped as much by listening as by treatment. In Thailand’s coastal town of Hua Hin, the pioneering wellness resort begins each retreat with a private health and wellness consultation and a Lifestyle Empowerment session, bringing together nutritionists, naturopaths, therapists, and mental wellness specialists to understand each guest’s needs before developing an individualized plan. Sixteen personalized retreats and more than 200 treatments draw on Thai Traditional Medicine and contemporary wellness practices, ranging from holistic gut health therapies to Watsu, a form of water therapy in which guests are gently supported and moved through warm water. With phones kept in guest rooms, the environment encourages a deliberate step away from daily distractions, while the guidance offered throughout a stay is designed to extend beyond the resort and into everyday life.

The Curated Take

The most meaningful measure of a wellness retreat may be what remains after departure. Chiva-Som’s emphasis on individual consultation and sustainable lifestyle changes moves the experience beyond temporary escape, placing the focus on understanding the body, cultivating healthier habits, and bringing that knowledge home. In a world where wellness is often packaged as a collection of treatments, the opportunity to be genuinely heard is a distinction worth noting.

item.title: Peru’s Wildest Landscapes Take Center Stage as Adventure Travel Destination of the Year
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From the Pacific coast to the high Andes and the Amazon rainforest, Peru has been named the Most Desirable Country for Adventure in the 2026 Wanderlust Reader Travel Awards, recognizing the remarkable range of landscapes and outdoor experiences found across the country. The award highlights opportunities well beyond the classic routes to Machu Picchu, including surfing along the northern coast, trekking through the snow-covered peaks of the Cordillera Blanca in Áncash, exploring the forests and waterfalls of Amazonas, and crossing the desert dunes surrounding Huacachina in Ica. Further afield, travelers can follow high-altitude routes around Ausangate, explore the Salkantay region or venture into the rainforest of Tambopata. Peru is also drawing attention through international sporting events such as the Ultra-Trail Cordillera Blanca and Adidas Andes Race, while PROMPERÚ’s Peru Outdoor Expo is connecting international travel professionals with emerging adventure experiences and destinations throughout the country.

The Curated Take

Peru’s appeal for adventure travelers extends beyond its iconic archaeological heritage. Its extraordinary geographic range creates opportunities to move between mountain trekking, desert exploration, coastal pursuits and rainforest encounters, often with a strong connection to local communities and landscapes. For travelers who have already experienced the familiar highlights, regions such as Áncash and Amazonas offer a compelling reason to return with a different perspective. The recognition also reinforces the value of looking beyond established itineraries to discover the many distinct journeys that make up Peru.

item.title: Where Music Meets Mindfulness in the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the peaceful Neyphu Valley near Paro, Bhutan Spirit Sanctuary is exploring the connections between creativity, cultural exchange and personal wellbeing through its Artists-in-Residence program. From October 28 to November 10, 2026, the intimate wellness retreat welcomes American singer, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Leven Kali, whose contemporary sound draws on R&B, soul and alternative influences. His visit coincides with the Asia Visionary Summit in Paro, where he has been invited to lecture and share his creative perspective. The residency offers an opportunity to experience Bhutan’s distinctive cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and natural surroundings while encouraging dialogue across creative disciplines. With just 24 rooms overlooking the valley, Bhutan Spirit Sanctuary provides a setting for a more contemplative approach to luxury travel, combining personalized wellness programs, Bhutanese traditional medicine and locally inspired cuisine.

The Curated Take

Bhutan offers a different kind of luxury travel experience, one shaped as much by cultural understanding and spiritual reflection as by its extraordinary mountain landscapes. Bhutan Spirit Sanctuary’s Artists-in-Residence program adds another dimension to that experience, creating space for international creative voices to engage with the country’s traditions and perspectives. The appeal extends beyond a conventional wellness retreat: it is an opportunity to encounter Bhutan through the exchange of ideas, artistic expression and a slower, more thoughtful relationship with place.

item.title: Can a Large Luxury Resort Be Truly Sustainable? Mulia Bali Is Setting a New Benchmark
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Luxury hospitality and environmental responsibility are increasingly expected to go hand in hand, and Mulia Bali is demonstrating what that can look like at scale. Across its three Nusa Dua properties and nine dining venues, the beachfront estate achieved a 99% landfill waste diversion rate during the first eight months of 2026, building on several years of steady progress in reducing its environmental footprint. The resort’s approach includes sorting waste across 15 operational categories, composting all green waste on-site, recovering glass for regional recycling and redirecting organic kitchen preparation waste to local agricultural partners. Plastic-free initiatives, cassava-based alternatives and water reclamation systems further contribute to its sustainability efforts. With 745 accommodations spanning private pool villas, all-suite stays and resort rooms, Mulia offers a notable example of how environmental stewardship can be integrated into the operations of a large-scale luxury resort in Bali.

The Curated Take

Sustainable travel is often associated with remote eco-lodges and small-scale retreats, but the environmental practices of major hospitality estates matter just as much. Mulia Bali’s progress is significant because it addresses the operational realities of luxury at scale, from dining and landscaping to guest accommodations and resource management. For travelers choosing a beachfront escape in Nusa Dua, the resort’s approach adds another dimension to the experience: a recognition that exceptional hospitality should also consider the long-term health of the destination in which it operates.

item.title: This Bali Villa Is Setting a New Standard for Private Luxury and Award-Winning Dining
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Bali’s luxury villa experience takes center stage with The AYANA Villa at AYANA Villas Bali, named Bali’s Leading Luxury Hotel Villa 2026 at the World Travel Awards. Set within the expansive AYANA Bali resort, the 3,000-square-meter, three-bedroom estate combines sweeping Indian Ocean views, lush tropical gardens, Balinese craftsmanship, and the privacy of a dedicated pool and personal butler service. Guests also enjoy priority access to the celebrated Rock Bar and the exclusive River Pool. Adding another distinction to the experience, DAVA Steak & Seafood, the villa property’s signature restaurant, earned a place among Tripadvisor’s 2026 Travelers’ Choice Awards: Best of the Best Restaurants & Food, recognizing it among the world’s top 25 fine dining restaurants. With its Argentine-inspired open-fire cooking, premium beef, line-caught seafood, and terrace dining overlooking Jimbaran Bay, DAVA extends the villa experience into an equally memorable culinary escape.

The Curated Take

The appeal of The AYANA Villa lies in the way it brings together several dimensions of a Bali stay without sacrificing privacy or a sense of place. Its generous scale and Balinese artistic details create an atmosphere rooted in the island, while the dedicated amenities and access to standout dining make it particularly compelling for milestone celebrations, multigenerational travel, and private gatherings. The recognition for both the villa and DAVA also highlights an important distinction: exceptional luxury is not only about the accommodations, but about the experiences that unfold around them.
